title: test-0019-SCI-PHY-FORCEPRESSURE
passage: In a bustling local market, a heavy wooden crate sits motionless on the concrete floor. Even though the crate is not moving, the Earth is constantly pulling it downward with gravity, while the floor pushes upward with an equal force, keeping it perfectly balanced. Nearby, a shopkeeper uses a sharp metal needle to sew a thick canvas bag. The needle easily pierces the fabric because its tip has a very small surface area, which concentrates the force to create high pressure. Meanwhile, a customer holds a strong magnet near a metal paperclip on the table. Without even touching the clip, the magnet pulls it across the surface. As the clip slides, a rough force called friction acts against the motion, even if the clip was initially at rest. Above them, the ceiling fan spins, pushing air molecules around. These invisible air molecules are constantly colliding with everything in the room, exerting atmospheric pressure from all directions, including sideways and upwards. This pressure is significant, but we do not feel crushed because the pressure inside our bodies pushes outward with equal strength, perfectly balancing the weight of the atmosphere pressing against our skin.
summary: These invisible air molecules are constantly colliding with everything in the room, exerting atmospheric pressure from all directions, including sideways and upwards. This pressure feels good, but we don't feel crushed because our body pushes against the atmosphere with equal strength.
